description: Provenance and publication-status records for artwork commissioned or selected for the Mature Feminine field guide.

records.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: full-bleed portrait illustration for a print field-guide spread, cropped to a 3.40 x 5.25 inch vertical frame
Primary request: portray the Closed Hearth, the passive shadow of bounded hospitality: privacy has hardened into exclusion, while a real capacity for chosen welcome remains recoverable
Scene/backdrop: an immaculate but unused interior sanctuary at twilight; a heavy closed door; a cold stone hearth with one faint coal; one empty chair near a carefully set but untouched place; a narrow warm line of light visible around the threshold
Subject: one adult woman, fully clothed, self-possessed and watchful rather than villainous, standing within the protected room; her posture conveys practiced withdrawal and guarded sovereignty
Style/medium: richly detailed painterly fantasy realism consistent with a mature archetype book; tactile stone, wood, wool, ash, and subtle floral motifs; elegant, psychologically symbolic, serious rather than melodramatic
Composition/framing: vertical 2:3 portrait, crop-safe central subject, visually strong from top to bottom, no important elements at extreme side edges; the doorway and hearth should read clearly in a narrow portrait crop
Lighting/mood: cool indigo and charcoal interior with restrained ember-gold at the threshold; quiet, sealed, lonely, dignified
Constraints: no text, captions, labels, borders, logos, watermarks, typography, deity names, sacred regalia, identifiable living-tradition cultural dress, children, visible abuse, or moralizing caricature
Avoid: glamorous seductress imagery, horror, witch clichés, locked-prison imagery, ruined or filthy domestic space, excessive blackness, photorealistic stock-photo look
records.editorialRationale: The closed threshold, cold hearth, unused place setting, and retained line of warm light show Privacy becoming enclosure without treating solitude or boundaries as pathology.
